query_text: Need a product launch site that actually feels like it was made with care, a web app where the hero section has a bold headline and one clean visual, the kind of thing that makes you stop scrolling, with a brief feature rundown below and a spot to sign up or get notified, the whole thing carrying that sense of occasion a real product launch deserves.

Create a campaign site that lives in a browser and carries its own identity, a focused web app built around one campaign with a strong visual at the top, a short message that actually says something, and a place for people to join or take action, the kind of site that feels like it was made with intention and not just assembled from a template.

Need a web app for an official brand store where customers can browse the full product lineup without jumping between five different pages, with a clean product listing, a search bar that actually works, and a straightforward way to add things to a cart and check out, so I stop losing people because the shopping flow is a mess.

Need a web app that handles both B2B and B2C orders in one place, so buyers can browse products, see pricing that adjusts based on whether they are a business or individual customer, and complete their order without me having to manually process everything, because right now managing two separate flows is killing my time.

Make a web app that collects sales leads with a simple form so potential customers can fill in their name, company, contact info, and what they are interested in, then saves everything in one place I can actually look at later, because right now leads come in through email and spreadsheets and it is a nightmare to track.

Create a web app for scheduling partnership discussions so a potential partner can pick a time slot, fill in basic details about their company and what they want to talk about, and get a confirmation, because right now coordinating meeting requests by email takes forever and things fall through the cracks.

Build a corporate learning center app for desktop browsers where employees can find all the company training content in one place, with courses organized by department or topic, a way to track which ones you have completed, and a simple search so you can find what you need without hunting through folders.

Need a web app for an employee training portal that lists all the available courses with a short description of each one, shows me which ones I have finished and which ones are still pending, and lets me filter by topic or job role so I can find the right training quickly, with a progress bar somewhere so I can see how far along I am overall.

Create a customer community web app where users can post questions, share tips, and reply to each other, with topics organized by category so it is easy to find discussions about the specific thing you are working on, and a profile for each member so you can see who is contributing and what they have posted before.

A user case study web app for desktop browsers where real customer stories are laid out one by one, each with a short summary of the problem they had, what they used to fix it, and what happened after, so visitors can browse by industry or outcome and find something that matches their own situation.

A customer self-service web app where users can log in, check their account status, submit a support request, and find answers to common questions all in one place, because right now customers have to email us for everything and it piles up fast, so having a browser-based tool they can use on their own would save everyone time.

Make a product configurator web app where a customer can pick a base product, choose from available options like size, color, or add-ons, see the updated price as they make selections, and then submit the configuration to request a quote, all running in the browser so the sales team does not have to walk every single person through it manually.

Make a funding and team introduction web app that actually has a point of view, something for desktop browsers that opens with a clear statement of what the company is building and why it matters, then introduces the team in a way that feels human rather than just a list of job titles, with a short section on where the company is headed and how to get in touch.

Build a brand site web app that has its own personality and does not look like every other startup site, something you open in a browser and immediately know what this company is about, with a strong visual language, a clean section that explains the product, and a tone that actually sounds like a real person wrote it.

Need a tech blog web app that feels like it has a real editorial identity and is not just a wall of posts, something in the browser where each article has room to breathe with good typography, articles are organized so returning readers can find older content by topic, and the whole thing reads like a place someone actually cares about.

Make a changelog web app that feels considered and worth reading, a browser-based tool where each update entry has a date, a short title, and a paragraph that actually explains what changed and why it matters, with older entries below so readers can scroll through the history and get a real sense of how the product has grown over time.

Need a SaaS product landing site that has a soul to it, a web app where the opening headline actually says something worth reading, features are described in plain language with just enough detail to make someone curious, there is a clear spot to sign up or try it, and the whole experience feels like it was designed by people who actually use the product themselves.

Build a pricing web app that is honest and easy to read, a browser-based tool where the different plans are laid out side by side with what is included in each one, a toggle for monthly versus yearly billing, and a short FAQ below for the questions people always ask before buying, the kind of pricing page that makes you feel like you are being treated like an adult.

Make a subscription purchase web app where a user can pick a plan, enter their payment details, and confirm their order in a few steps without being bounced between multiple pages, because right now the checkout process is slow and confusing and people are dropping off before they finish, so I need something in the browser that just works cleanly end to end.

An add-on services purchase web app for desktop browsers where existing customers can see the extra features or packages available to them, pick what they want, and pay for it right there, so they can upgrade on their own without having to contact support and wait for someone to manually process the change.

Build a demo booking web app where a potential customer can pick a date and time that works for them, fill in their name, company, and what they want to see in the demo, and get a confirmation with next steps, because right now scheduling demos involves too much back and forth over email and I lose people before the meeting even happens.

Need a web app for scheduling sales conversations where a lead can choose an available time slot, leave a short note about what they want to discuss, and get a confirmation right away, because chasing people back and forth to find a meeting time is eating up hours every week and I need a browser-based tool that just handles the scheduling part automatically.

Make a product documentation web app for desktop browsers that has a left-side list of all the topics so you can jump to what you need without scrolling forever, a search bar at the top so you can type a keyword and find the right article fast, and each article laid out clearly with headings and code examples where needed.

Need a web app for a tutorial and learning center where courses are grouped by topic or skill level, each one has a clear list of what you will learn, you can track which lessons you have finished, and there is a way to search for specific topics without having to scroll through everything, all running in the browser so it is easy to access from any desktop.

Create a user forum web app for desktop browsers where people can start threads, reply to each other, and vote on helpful answers, with topics organized into categories so conversations about different things do not get mixed together, and a simple way to search for existing threads before posting a new question.
